subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: GPU type / throughput targets
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hernandez <alex.hernandez@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-05T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: GPU type / throughput targets

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + our asks so we can put together a tailored dedicated capacity proposal: 

Recap from call:
- ACME plans to move real-time recommendation and search ranking to Redwood Dedicated.
- Expected 2 models in prod initially: a 3B causal model (context up to 2k tokens) and a 7B encoder-decoder for reranking.
- Peak qps target: ~200 requests/sec (p95 latency target <= 200ms for small seqs).
- Monthly token volume estimate (aggregate): 120M input tokens + 380M output tokens = 500M tokens/month.
- Current target unit economics: ~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens (budget range for evaluation/proof-of-value).

What we need to confirm from your side to finalize pricing: 
1) Preferred GPU type: H100 (higher perf) vs A100 (cost-efficient). Any preference or existing infra constraints?
2) Reservation size: are you thinking in node/GPU count (e.g., 8x A100 GPUs) or throughput targets (tokens/sec)?
3) Percent of traffic that needs hard latency SLO vs best-effort (i.e., what fraction needs <200ms p95)?
4) Contract term / budget expectations for reserved capacity (monthly commit range) — helps us size discounts.

Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v3.pdf (baseline pricing tiers) and perf-report-A100-vs-H100.pdf (high-level perf differences).

Next steps: if you can reply to the 4 items above, Marcus will draft a proposal with two options (A100 cost-optimized and H100 high-throughput) and rough $/1M token targets. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up tomorrow if useful.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Hernandez <alex.hernandez@acmeretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2027-08-05T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: GPU type / throughput targets

Thanks Dylan — good summary. A few answers inline below.

> 1) Preferred GPU type: H100 (higher perf) vs A100 (cost-efficient). Any preference or existing infra constraints?
We don't have an infra preference yet. Our infra team has recommended starting with A100s for cost reasons but we've seen better perf on H100 in benchmarks. Open to both options in the proposal.

> 2) Reservation size: are you thinking in node/GPU count (e.g., 8x A100 GPUs) or throughput targets (tokens/sec)?
We think in throughput goals. Target steady-state throughput: ~6,000 tokens/sec aggregate across both models. Peak burst to 10,000 tokens/sec.

> 3) Percent of traffic that needs hard latency SLO vs best-effort (i.e., what fraction needs <200ms p95)?
About 60% of traffic (the recommendation and search paths) need hard latency SLO (<200ms p95). The reranking is OK to be best-effort at higher latencies for now.

> 4) Contract term / budget expectations for reserved capacity (monthly commit range) — helps us size discounts.
We're evaluating a 6–12 month pilot with a budget aiming for total spend ~$95k–$140k/month. That should guide your committed capacity recommendations.

We attached our expected traffic pattern and a sample request distribution — see Acme_capacity_proposal.xlsx.

If you and Marcus can draft two options (A100 cost-optimized, H100 performance), that'd be perfect. Can we get a proposal by EOD Friday?

- Alex
Director, ML Platforms | Acme Retail

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hernandez <alex.hernandez@acmeretail.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-05T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: GPU type / throughput targets

Alex — thanks for the fast responses and the attachment. A quick engineering read from our side to translate throughput into GPU sizing so pricing is more concrete: 

Engineering estimate (ballpark):
- For the 3B causal model (avg seq ~120 tokens per request): expect ~1,200 tokens/sec per A100 GPU (batched, KV cache effective). H100 ~1.6x that (so ~1,920 tokens/sec).
- For the 7B reranker (shorter sequences, heavier compute): estimate ~900 tokens/sec per A100, ~1,400 tokens/sec per H100.

Sizing to meet steady-state 6,000 tokens/sec (split approximated 70% causal / 30% rerank):
- A100-only option: need ~5 A100 GPUs (safety factor 1.2 → propose 6 A100 GPUs).
- H100-only option: need ~3 H100 GPUs (safety factor 1.2 → propose 4 H100 GPUs).

To cover peak bursts to 10,000 tokens/sec, we recommend either:
- Burst pool (on-demand GPUs) for spikes, or
- Larger reservation: A100 plan → 10 GPUs; H100 plan → 6 GPUs.

Estimated cost guidance (rough):
- A100 reserved: ballpark $85k–$110k / month for 6–10 GPU reservation (depending on discount/term).
- H100 reserved: ballpark $120k–$160k / month for 4–6 GPU reservation.

Unit economics mapping (approx $/1M tokens):
- A100 (6 GPU plan, with caching/batching): ~$900 / 1M tokens (within your target).
- H100 (4 GPU plan): ~$1,150 / 1M tokens (higher perf, higher $).

We'll attach a formal proposal with exact line items, and two scenarios (pilot 6-month commit vs 12-month commit) showing discounts to hit your target budget of $95k–$140k/month.

Proposed next steps:
- We'll circulate a 2-page option sheet (A100 vs H100) + recommended reserve sizes by EOD Friday.
- If you want, schedule a 30-min technical sync with our infra lead to validate perf assumptions (Marcus + Marissa + your infra lead).

-Marсus
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
